L0: A diagnostic test run that checks whether many copies of the same automated task, run at once against a shared environment, interfere with each other through shared infrastructure.
L1: A diagnostic test run that checks whether many copies of the same automated task interfere with each other through shared infrastructure. It works by launching a large number of identical parallel copies (for example, 500 runs) of the same task against a shared execution environment, such as a staging or shared cluster, and watching whether separate worker instances collide over shared resources. It specifically detects interference caused by infrastructure that is not uniquely named per worker, such as scratch-file, temporary-directory, or cache naming that is shared across workers on the same host or cluster, causing one worker to read or write another's files.
L2: A diagnostic test run that checks whether many copies of the same automated task interfere with each other through shared infrastructure. It launches a large number of identical parallel copies (for example, 500 runs) of one task against a shared execution environment (staging or a shared cluster) and detects cross-instance interference from infrastructure that is not uniquely named per worker, such as temporary-directory or cache naming that collides across workers on the same host or cluster. It produces a contamination rate, read as the percentage of runs affected (for example, 6%, 11%, or 4%) — the fraction showing shared-state interference, like reading or writing another worker's scratch or cache files. It applies to batched or parallel execution harnesses and should be run on any such harness before trusting behavioral metrics from it, especially when results are sensitive to file state. The rate is expected to shrink after isolation fixes but not reach zero when workers share underlying infrastructure, like a common cache layer, by design.
